REPORT
Date Oct. 27th, 19 31

Subject (in full) Further report regarding Functioning of Anti-Japanese Boycott Party in Ying Ziang Kong Village on 11-6-31. File D. 2588/3.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Wardrop.

Sir,
Further enquiry in the above matter at the Yi Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop, No. 4b Ward Road, who are the actual owners of the three bales of cotton goods seized, and at the Dong Sing Dyeing Company Ying Ziang Kong Village, from whose cart the goods were actually seized on 11-6-31, was made on 27-10-31, when it was ascertained that neither of the above shops had heard anything further from the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association, nor had they approached the Association with a view to getting the goods returned.

The owners of the two shops have agreed to settle the matter of the loss of the goods value $540.00 between themselves, by Ts Ching Loong, owner of the Dyeing Shop, giving up all claim to the $200.00 owed him by the Yi Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop for work done by him and in addition has paid $30.00. Thus Ts Ching Loong's share of the loss is $230.00 and Zau Ts Kui, owner of the piece goods shop bears the loss of the remaining $310.00, and has also agreed to continue to send his work to be done at Ts Ching Loong's Dyeing Shop.

The matter of settling who is to be responsible for the loss now appears to have been amicably settled between the parties.

I am, Sir,
R. Wardrop,
D.S.I.

主题（全称） 关于1931年6月11日英商公和纱厂村（Ying Ziang Kong Village）抵制日货会活动情况的进一步报告。档案号 D. 2588/3。

由副督察长沃德罗普（Wardrop）制作并呈报。

先生，
就上述事项，于1931年10月27日对华德路4b号义松祥布店（Yi Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop，该店为被扣押的三包棉布的实际货主）以及英商公和纱厂村的东盛染坊（Dong Sing Dyeing Company，货物实际于1931年6月11日从该店的车上被扣押）进行了进一步调查。经查实，上述两家店铺均未再收到抵制日货会的任何消息，也未为了追回货物而主动联系该会。

两家店铺的店主已同意自行解决价值540.00美元的货物损失问题，由染坊店主朱金龙（Ts Ching Loong）放弃义松祥布店欠他的200.00美元加工费债权，此外还支付了30.00美元。因此，朱金龙承担的损失份额为230.00美元，布店店主赵子庚（Zau Ts Kui）承担剩余的310.00美元损失，并同意继续将其织物送往朱金龙的染坊进行加工。

目前看来，关于由谁负责赔偿损失的问题已在各方之间友好解决。

此致，
R. 沃德罗普（Wardrop），
副督察长。

Sir,
Zau Ts Kau was further interviewed at No.45 Ward Road as
regards the action he contemplated taking against Ts Ching Loong
in order to recover the value of the goods which were seized by
the Anti-Japanese Association.
No definite reply was received from him further than he
had not yet decided to take any action, but the fact that he
owes Ts Ching Loong about $200.00 for work done is so much in
his favour, as he does not contemplate paying it meantime.
Attached herewith is the receipt received from the Anti-
Japanese Association on 6-9-31 for the three bales of cotton
seized (Large Receipt).
Small bill was received on 18-9-31 from Zau Ts Kau
proprietor of the Nyi Tsoong Ziang Piece Goods shop No.45

"Five Sycee" brand cotton cloth delivered to No.45 Ward Road by
the Zuh Sing Tsung (日新增) Piece Goods Shop, Rue du Consulate
on 17-7-31.

Sir,

On 16-9-31, Ts Ching Loong, master of the Dong Sing Dyeing Co., Ying Ziang Kong, O.O.L. not having received any reply to his letter of 7-9-31 to the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association, visited the Association Offices at the Temple of Heaven, North Honan Road.

In the above office, he was handed a letter, and also told that there had been a meeting of 36 members of the Association, who had decided that, as the goods were of Japanese origin, they must be confiscated.

The letter given Ts Ching Loong, on being translated, read as follows:-

"Your letter requesting the return of the 'Five Sycee' "brand cloth and expressing willingness to be fined "was received.

"The matter has been placed before the General Meeting "of this Society, and it was decided to refuse your "application.

"If you find yourself in difficulty of any description "you may report same to us.

Chopped The Anti-Japanese Association"

Ts Ching Loong, questioned regarding the meaning of the last paragraph of the letter, stated he was informed verbally that it meant, if he had any trouble with the master of the Nyi Tsoong Ziang Piece Goods Shop, owner of the goods seized, he was to refer the matter to the above Association.

On 17-9-31, C.D.S.I. Ah Zien together with Tsau Tsung Yeu (趙仲漁), assistant of Ts Ching Loong (朱金龍), took the letter to the Piece Goods shop, No.45 Ward Road and showed the

Subject (in full) Further report regarding Functioning of Anti-Japanese Boycott Party in Ying Ziang Kong Village on 11-8-31.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Wardrop.

Sir,
Further enquiry made into the circumstances of the actual seizure of the three bales of cloth revealed the following.
No actual violence or threats were used at the Dong Sing Dyeing Co, Ying Ziang Kong, O.O.L., before the Dyeshop master disclosed where the goods were placed in his assistants home behind No. J.G. 640 Ying Ziang Kong Village, but owing to the presence of a large number of workers of the San Yeu Towel Factory, Moh Yeu San Road, O.O.L., the dyeshop master Ts Ching Loong (朱金龍) was afraid of injury or damage to his property if he did not disclose where the goods were hidden.
After the seizure the goods were taken to the road way outside the above factory premises and later removed, believed by motor car.
On 5-9-31 C.D.S.I. Ah Zien succeeded in ascertaining that the names of five persons who signed the receipt for the property were on the books of the office of the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association at North Honan Road, and although it was stated that they lived on the premises, this he could not definitely find out.
On 6-9-31, C.D.S.I. Ah Zien, and C.D.S. 85 Bang Say Ching, accompanied by Ts Ching Loong of the Dong Sing Dye Shop, proceeded to No. 45 Ward Road in order to ask the shop master Zau Ta Kan, to accompany them to the 5th Division of the Public Safety Bureau at Poashan Road, Chapei, to ask for assistance in making enquiries at No. 99 West Poashing Li, Poashan Road. Zau Ta Kan (赵了样) refused to accompany Detectives but detailed his shop assistant Shu Ching Sung (许金章).
At the Public Safety Bureau at Poashan Road C.D.S.I. Ah Zien explained the purpose of the visit and asked for an escort to

由副督察长沃德罗普（Wardrop）制作并呈报。

先生，
对三包布料被实际扣押的情况进行的进一步调查揭示了以下事实。
在东盛染坊（位于英商公和纱厂村 O.O.L.），在染坊主披露货物藏匿在其助手家中（位于英商公和纱厂村 J.G. 640号后面）之前，并未使用实际的暴力或威胁，但由于摩耶山路（Moh Yeu San Road，O.O.L.）三友毛巾厂（San Yeu Towel Factory）的大量工人在场，染坊主朱金龙（朱金龍）担心如果不披露货物藏匿地点，其人身或财产会受到伤害或损坏。
扣押后，货物被带到上述工厂门外的道路上，随后被运走，据信是用汽车运走的。
1931年9月5日，华人副督察阿先（Ah Zien）成功查明了在货物收据上签名的五个人的名字列在北河南路抵制日货会办事处的名册上，尽管据说这些人住在该处，但他无法确切查明这一点。
1931年9月6日，华人副督察阿先和华人警员85号邦赛清（Bang Say Ching）在东盛染坊朱金龙的陪同下，前往华德路45号，请求店主赵达堪（Zau Ta Kan）陪同他们前往闸北宝山路公共安全局第五分局，请求协助在宝山西波兴里99号进行调查。赵达堪（赵了样）拒绝陪同侦探，但指派了其店员许金章（Shu Ching Sung）。
在宝山路的公共安全局，华人副督察阿先说明了来意，并要求派员护送前往

Woo Yuen Foo then told the detectives and shop master to take
the receipt to the Head Office at the Temple of Heaven, North

At the Temple of Heaven the party met one Dzung Kyi Foo
(鄭劍伯) who examined the receipt and told Ts Ching Loong that
he required a letter giving details of ownership, date and
place where the goods were bought, and that he would send the
letter to Nantao to the (Koumingtong Party Head Office) where
enquiries would be made as to the conditions under which the
goods could be returned.

Ts Ching Loong sent a letter to the Anti-Japanese Boycott
Association Office on 7-9-31 and is meantime awaiting further
developments.

I am, Sir,

It does not appear that there is sufficient evidence to prefer a charge under Article 318 of the Criminal Code. There is no evidence of the identity of the persons seizing the goods; neither is there any evidence of violence or threats. A prosecution cannot be instituted against the Anti-Japanese Association as a whole, but must be instituted against the individuals committing criminal acts.

If the identity of the persons seizing the goods can be established and some proof of violence or threats obtained, a charge might be preferred.

Sir,
Upon being asked for assistance in securing the restoration of three bales of cloth which were seized in the Settlement by five anti-Japanese pickets on August 11, 1931 Colonel Chen Hai Tseng, Chief of the Public Safety Bureau, gave the following reply on August 25:-
"I am sorry that I am unable to render any assistance in this case because the anti-Japanese Association pays no heed to my advice. I have received many complaints of this nature but I am powerless. Personally I desire to have the anti-Japanese Association dissolved. It has even disobeyed the order issued by the National Government the other day directing it to return to Japanese owners their respective goods seized. I think that the Municipal Police should either arrest the pickets if located or give a warning to the anti-Japanese Association whose office is located in the Settlement."
It was pointed out to Col. Chen that although the office of the anti-Japanese Association is in the Settlement, it was situated in the premises of the Temple of the Queen of Heaven and therefore under his jurisdiction to which he made no reply.

杨树浦巡捕房，
日期：1931年8月12日。

主题（全称）：引翔港村内日本抵制团的活动。

由副警司斯科特 (D.P.S. Scott) 撰写，由 [空白] 转呈

先生，
1931年8月11日晚上11点，居住在华德路45号的店主赵鹤鸣 (Zeu Hwo King) 与一名在同兴 (Dong Sing) 染坊（位于引翔港，越界筑路区）受雇的苦力赵仲舆 (Tsau Tsung You) 一同来到巡捕房，报告称在1931年8月11日晚上约7点，几名日本抵制团成员前往后者位于引翔港村 C36-9 号场所后方的住所，并从那里拿走了3个包裹，每个包裹装有15卷白棉布（日本制造），总价值为450.00美元。
经本人及华籍侦探警长 (C.D.Cs) 181号和307号调查，查明赵鹤鸣与同兴染坊有合同关系，1931年8月11日下午2点，该公司代表曾拜访他，询问是否有材料需要染色。由于上述布匹需要染色，他给予了肯定答复，结果是1931年8月11日下午4点30分，染坊的两名苦力来到华德路45号，接管了这3个包裹。
按照他们的主人朱金龙 (Ts Ching Loong) 收到的指示，他们没有直接将包裹送往工厂，而是将其送到赵仲舆的家中，并将包裹留在那里。
本人及华籍侦探警长181号和307号随后前往引翔港村，并在那里与朱金龙取得联系。他被带到本巡捕房，他表示由于对日本货物的抵制，他命令三名苦力将材料送到赵仲舆家中。他还表示，1931年8月11日下午6点，5名日本抵制团成员来到他的工厂，搜查场所以寻找

REPORT

Yangtsepoo Station,
Date Aug. 26 1931.

Subject (in full) Further report regarding Functioning of Anti-Japanese
Boycott Party in Ying Ziang Kong Village on 11-8-31.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I, Wardrop

Sir,

Further to the original report made on 12-8-31 in regard
to the seizure of goods in Ying Ziang Kong village by members of
Anti-Japanese Boycott Association, two visits have been made to
Ying Ziang Kong Sub- Station of the Public Safety Bureau.

From enquiries made from Inspector Woo Nyoh Ding (吳玉亭)
his Secretary and Sergeants stationed there, it was ascertained that
whilst no complaint had been made by the owner of the Dong Sing
Dyeing Coy., Chapel, or the Nyih Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop,
No.45 Ward Road, (H. Police) they were aware of the search of the premises of
the Dong Sing Dyeing Coy., and home of Tsau Tsung Yue (趙仲漢),
and the seizure of the goods. Had a complaint been received, it
would have been forwarded to Headquarters of the Public Safety
Bureau. The Inspector states he would have detained the Anti-
Japanese pickets, the complainant and the goods and asked for
instructions from his superior. The whole attitude of the Ying
Ziang Kong Native Police is that the Anti-Japanese Association is
recognized by the Koumintang Party of Shanghai, whom they regard
as their superiors; and are unwilling to interfere, not having
received definite orders. Inspector in charge unable to assist
in recovery of property seized.

Enquiry has also been made from Ts Ching Loong, Proprietor
of the Dong Sing Dyeing Co. Ying Ziang Kong, O.O.L. He states that
about 9 a.m. 12-8-31, he visited the Anti-Japanese Boycott Asso-
ciation Offices in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Honan
Road.

In the office of above Association, he met the five members
of the picket who made the seizure of the cotton cloth and searched
his premises on 11-8-31.

主题（全称） 关于1931年8月11日英商公和祥村（Ying Ziang Kong Village）反日抵制会活动情况的进一步报告。

由副督察长沃德罗普（Wardrop）撰写并呈送

先生：

继1931年8月12日就反日抵制会成员在英商公和祥村扣押货物一事提交的初步报告之后，本人已两次前往公安局英商公和祥分所进行查访。

经向该分所督察吴玉亭（Woo Nyoh Ding）、其秘书及驻守警士查询，获悉虽然同兴染坊（Dong Sing Dyeing Coy.）、教堂或华德路45号（H区警政辖区）义昌祥布店（Nyih Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop）的店主并未提出投诉，但他们知晓对同兴染坊及赵仲汉（Tsau Tsung Yue）住所的搜查以及货物被扣押的情况。若收到投诉，本应转呈公安局总局。该督察称，若有投诉，他本会扣留反日纠察队员、投诉人及货物，并向上级请示指示。英商公和祥华捕的整体态度是，鉴于上海国民党承认反日协会，且华捕视国民党为上级，在未接到明确命令的情况下，他们不愿介入。负责督察无法协助追回被扣财产。

此外，还向英商公和祥同兴染坊业主查景龙（Ts Ching Loong，O.O.L.）进行了查询。他陈述称，1931年8月12日上午9时许，他曾前往位于北河南路上海总商会内的反日抵制会办事处。

在上述协会的办事处内，他会见了五名参与1931年8月11日搜查其场所并扣押棉布的纠察队员。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zau Ts-kau (赵子庚)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S.I. Montgomery
at 45 Ward Road on the 16-8-31 and interpreted by Clerk Liao Tsong Chien.

My name is Zau Ts-kau (赵子庚), aged 64 years, married
native of Shanghai. I am the proprietor of the Nyi Tsoong Tsiang
Piece Goods Shop (义昌祥) 45 Ward Road. The Dong Sing Dyeing
Company (同兴) also known as the Yue Zeng Zang Company (裕增昌)
38 Ying Ziang Kong, does a considerable amount of cloth dyeing
for my firm and has a guarantee bond with me to make good any
of my cloth entrusted to them and lost.

On August 11, 1931 at about 3.30 p.m. I saw two coolies
bring to the shop a bale of cloth on a hand trolley. One of
these coolies is known to me as an employee of the Dong Sing
Company. He is known by the nick-name "Ah Goong" (阿公) the foolish
man. The bale of cloth was delivered to my shop and "Ah Goong"
asked me if there was any more work for the Dong Sing Company.
I said that there was, and asked "Ah Goong" how many bales he
could take. He answered that he could take three bales there-
fore, I instructed my assistants to give the two coolies three
bales of Japanese white cloth, marked "Five Syces" (五元宝),
there was also some foreign writing on the bales. I said I want-
ed the cloth dyed black. The three bales were placed on the
hand trolley and I made an entry in "Ah Goong's" book but did
not get a receipt. The value of the three bales is $550.00.
At about 4 p.m. "Ah Goong" and his companion left the premises.
At about 7.30 p.m. the same day, a man who said he was the son
of the proprietor of the Dong Sing Company, came to my shop on
a bicycle, and reported to me that my three bales of cloth,
those taken away by "Ah Goong" had been discovered by the Anti-
Japanese Association and it was suggested that we should send

1931年8月11日下午3时30分左右，我看见两名苦力用手推车将一包布运到店里。其中一名苦力我认识，是同兴公司的雇员，绰号叫“阿公”（Ah Goong，意为傻瓜）。这包布送到我店后，“阿公”问我同兴公司是否还有活干。我说有，并问“阿公”能拉几包。他回答说能拉三包，于是我便吩咐助手给这两名苦力三包日本白布，标记为“五元宝”（Five Syces），布包上还有一些外文。我说我要把布染成黑色。这三包布被放在手推车上，我在“阿公”的本子上做了登记，但没有开具收据。这三包布价值550.00美元。下午4点左右，“阿公”和他的同伴离开了店铺。当天晚上7点30分左右，一个自称是同兴公司店主儿子的人骑自行车来到我店里，向我报告说，我那三包被“阿公”拉走的布已被反日协会发现，并建议我们派人

On August 11, 1931 at about 3.30 p.m. I was in the shop when

One of these men is known to me as a coolie named "Ah Goong" (阿
同興染坊
憨), employed by the Dong Sing Dyeing Company at Ying Hsiang
Kong; the other man is unknown to me. I did not hear what was

My name is Wei Nyeu-sung, aged 23, married, native of Kiangsu

At about 3.30 p.m. on August 11, two coolies, one of which
is, known to me as "Ah Goong", (阿恭) an employee of the
Dong Sing Dyeing Company, Ying Ziang Kong, (which does dye-
ing work for our firm) came to our shop with a bale of
cloth which had been dyed for us. It was brought on a
small hand-trolley. After delivering the bale "Ah Goong"

本人名为桓允快，现年 23 岁，已婚，江苏籍。
本人在 Ward Road 45 号的义昌祥洋货号（Nyi Tsoong Tsiang Piece Goods Shop）任职店员，在此已工作九年，期间在此完成学徒期。店主名为赵子庚（Tsau Ts Kau）。
1931 年 8 月 11 日下午约 3 时 30 分，两名苦力来到本店，其中一人本人认识，名为“阿恭”（Ah Goong），系同兴染坊（Ying Ziang Kong，该厂为本店进行染色加工）的雇员。他们用手推车运来一捆为本店染好的布料。交付这捆布料后，“阿恭”询问是否还有布料需要染色。“阿恭”说，由于现在染色工作在租界内进行，他们可以承接各种业务。本店东主说他有一些布料需要染色，并问“阿恭”能带走多少捆。“阿恭”回答他和同伴可以带走三捆。本店东主指示将标记为“五元宝”的三捆布料放置在手推车上。此事办妥后，刚过下午 4 时，“阿恭”及其助手离开店铺。
1931 年 8 月 11 日晚刚过 7 时，一名男子来到本店，本人不知其姓名，但得知他是同兴公司老板的儿子。他说他刚从同兴公司过来，那里有三四十名反日纠察队员发现了那三捆布料并欲予扣押。他说我们最好派人去与他们谈谈。

My name is Tsau Tsung-yue aged 50 married Native of Shaoshing.
For the last fourteen years I have been employed by the Deng
Sing Dyeing Company (同興染坊), No. 38 Ying Ziang Kong situated
in Chinese Territory, and the Proprietor is named Ts Ching Leong
(朱金龍). I am now head assistant of this firm. I live in
a small room of an unnumbered house located to the rear of No.
640 Ying Ziang Kong, which is within Settlement Limits.
At about 2 p.m. on August 11, 1931 I heard the
proprietor instruct two of our coolies, named Zau Ah-sze (趙河水)
and Zee Ah-kung 徐阿根, to deliver some finished cloth to the Ngi Tseong
Ziang (義昌祥) Piece Goods Shop, 45, Ward Road and at the same
time to ask that shop if there was any more cloth to be dyed,
and if there was any it was to be taken to my house which is
within the Settlement Limits. I saw Zee Ah-kung leave the shop
shortly afterwards . My master has, on other occasion, stored
cloth at my house, but this has been usually done when there was
too much stock in the shop.
I left the Dong Sing Company and arrived at my home
at 3.30 p.m. August 11, and about 5 p.m. the two coolies came to
my house accompanied by the master and having three bales of
cloth on the hand trolley. I estimated the weights of the bales
as about 200 lbs each. On each bale there was some foreign
writing and also a trade-mark "Five Sycee" (五元寶). The coolies
placed the three bales in my room. The master and the coolies
then left the house . I remained behind to lock up. When I
had done so I went back to the Dong Sing Company arriving there
at about 5.30 p.m.

我叫赵仲岳，50岁，已婚，籍贯绍兴。
过去十四年间，我受雇于位于华界的英翔公路38号同兴染坊（ Deng Sing Dyeing Company (同興染坊) ），店主名叫朱金龙（ Ts Ching Leong (朱金龍) ）。我现任该商号的高级职员。我住在英翔公路640号后面一所无门牌号码的房屋的一间小屋里，该处位于租界范围内。
1931年8月11日下午2点左右，我听见店主指示我们要两名苦力，名叫赵河水（ Zau Ah-sze (趙河水) ）和徐阿根（ Zee Ah-kung 徐阿根 ），将一些成品布匹送至华德路45号的义昌祥（ Ngi Tseong Ziang (義昌祥) ）布庄，并同时询问该店是否有更多布匹需要染色，如果有，就运到我在租界范围内的家中。我随后看见徐阿根离开店铺。我的主人以前也曾将布匹存放在我家，但这通常是在店内库存过多时才会这样做。
我离开东兴公司，于1931年8月11日下午3时30分到达家中，大约下午5时，两名苦力陪同主人来到我家，手推车上载有三包布匹。我估计每包布匹重约200磅。每包布匹上都有外文标记以及“五元宝”（ Five Sycee (五元寶) ）商标。苦力们将这三包布匹放进我的房间。随后主人和苦力们离开了房子。我留下来锁门。锁好门后，我返回东兴公司，大约在下午5时30分到达那里。

At about 6 p.m. the same day five men on wearing foreign
dress, entered the Dong Sing Company and asked for the master.
I asked them what did they want with the master and they said
they were members of an Anti-Japanese Association the office of
which was located in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building.
I then asked them their reason for coming and they answered
that they had received information that our firm was in possession
of Japanese goods, and forthwith conducted a search of the shop
I did not see the pickets wearing badges but they produced a
piece of cloth with some writing on it, the purport of which I do not
know. Ts Ching-loong then admitted to the five men that he
was the proprietor (At that time I noticed about 30 coolies out
side the shop). The shop master said there were no Japanese
goods on the premises. The five men then said that they only
wanted to inspect the goods. At about 6.30 p.m. the master
instructed me to lead the five men to my house to show them the
the bales but pointed out that if the pickets wanted to remove
them they must inform the owner. The pickets refused to lea-
ve in a body but instead, they sent one of their number along
with over ten of the coolies. I showed the men the three
bales and the member of the anti-Japanese Association instruct-
ed the coolies to remove the bales. I remonstrated with
them, pointing out that they had said they only wanted to look
at the bales. The picket told me it was none of my business
and all Japanese goods had to be confiscated. The coolies
carried the bales away to a place near my house but in Chinese
territory. I did not follow them but stood and watched.

native of Shaoshing taken by me D. S. I. Montgomery

My name is Zau Ah-sze (趙阿水) aged 28, married, native of
Shaoshing. I am employed in the Dong Sing Dyeing Company
(同兴) 38 Ying Hsiang Kong, O.O.L. I reside at an unnumbered
house opposite the Dong Sing Company of which Ts Ching Loong (朱金龍)
is the proprietor. At 2 p.m. on August 11, 1931 I heard the
proprietor tell Zee Ah-kung (徐阿根), a coolie employed by the Dong Sing
Company to take a bale of finished cloth to the Nyi Tsoong Ziang (義昌祥)
Piece Goods Shop, 45 Ward Road, and if they had any more cloth
to be dyed to bring it back. I was told to meet Zee Ah-kung
and help him in case there was any cloth brought back.
Zee Ah-kung put the bale on a hand trolley and left almost
immediately. About one hour later I left the Dong Sing
Company and proceeded to Ward and Lay Roads corner where I waited
and after a little time I saw Zee Ah-kung and another man push-
ing the hand trolley, upon which were three bales of cloth,
along the road. I went to their assistance and the three of
us pulled the hand trolley to the house of Tsau Tsung-yue, (趙仲悅)
the senior assistant of the Dong Sing Company. When we arrived
there Zee Ah-kung left us to call Ts Ching Loong. Myself and
Zee Ah-kung's friend watched the three bales of cloth. In a
little time Zee Ah-kung returned accompanied by Ts Ching Loong
The latter saw that the three bales were properly placed in Tsau
Tsung-yue's house. Tsau was in the house at the time cooking
some food. After having seen the bales placed in proper order
Ts Ching Loong, Zee Ah-kung's friend, and myself returned to the
Dong Sing Company, and shortly afterwards Tsau Tsung-yue follow-
ed us.

我叫赵阿水（Zau Ah-sze），28岁，已婚，原籍绍兴。我受雇于位于外马路（O.O.L.）引翔港38号的同兴染坊（Dong Sing Dyeing Company）。我居住在对面一所无门牌号的房屋内，该染坊由朱金龙（Ts Ching Loong）经营。1931年8月11日下午2点，我听到店主吩咐同兴染坊的苦力徐阿根（Zee Ah-kung）将一包成品布送至华德路45号的义昌祥（Nyi Tsoong Ziang）布店，如果他们有更多需要染色的布料，就带回来。我被告知去接应徐阿根，以防有布料带回时协助他。
徐阿根将布包放在手推车上，随即离开。大约一小时后，我离开同兴染坊，前往华德路与雷氏路（Lay Roads）拐角处等待，过了一会儿，我看见徐阿根和另一名男子推着手推车沿路走来，车上有三包布。我上前协助，我们三人将手推车拉至同兴染坊高级职员赵仲悦（Tsau Tsung-yue）的家中。到达那里后，徐阿根离开我们去叫朱金龙。我和徐阿根的朋友看守着这三包布。不久，徐阿根陪同朱金龙返回。后者确认三包布已妥善放置在赵仲悦的屋内。当时赵仲悦正在屋内做饭。确认布匹摆放整齐后，朱金龙、徐阿根的朋友和我返回同兴染坊，不久后赵仲悦也跟随我们回来。

At about 6 p.m. the same day five men followed by a number
of labourers, came to the Dong Sing Dyeing Company.
The five men entered the shop and asked for Mr. Tsau.
They told Mr. Tsau that they were members of the Anti-Japanese
Association and they had received information that he had
received three bales of Japanese cloth. The master told them
that it would be better to take the matter up with the owner
of the cloth. The five men said that they only wanted to
see it, whereupon the master told Tsau to lead them (The Anti-
Japanese pickets) to Tsau's house. I do not know how many
of the pickets went to Tsau's house but some of them remained
in the Dong Sing Company. The picket or pickets who went
to Tsau's house were accompanied by about ten of the labourers
who were outside the shop. After a little time the pickets
and the labourers returned and Tsau told the shop master that
the pickets had taken the three bales away. The pickets
told Ts Ching Loong, that if he wanted the three bales back he
must apply to the Anti-Japanese Association and stated the
address. The Anti-Japanese pickets them left the shop.
The Anti-Japanese pickets were not wearing uniform but had bad-
ges. As far as I know they were unarmed.

The above statement has been read over to me and is correct.

(Signed) Zau Ah-sze.
Witnessed by Clerk Liao Tsong Chien.

当天傍晚6点左右，五名男子在一群劳工的跟随下来到同兴染坊。
这五人进入店内，指名要找赵先生。他们告诉赵先生，他们是反日协会的成员，并收到情报称他接收了三包日本布匹。店主告诉他们，最好与布匹所有者交涉此事。这五人说他们只想看一看，于是店主让赵仲悦带领他们（反日纠察队）前往赵的住所。我不知道有多少纠察队员去了赵的住所，但有些人留在了同兴染坊。前往赵住所的纠察队员由店外的大约十名劳工陪同。过了一会儿，纠察队员和劳工们返回，赵仲悦告诉店主，纠察队已将那三包布带走。纠察队员告诉朱金龙，如果他想要回那三包布，必须向反日协会申请，并留下了地址。随后，反日纠察队离开了店铺。
反日纠察队未穿制服，但佩戴徽章。据我所知，他们未携带武器。
